market_summary: Markets are jittery around AI capex sustainability even as cloud growth prints remain exceptional: AWS (+39% YoY) and Google Cloud (+103% YoY) both beat, yet Meta's stock and credit outlook are under pressure from S&P's negative revision on ballooning ~$135-145B annual capex plans. US indices sold off broadly today (SPY -1.8%, QQQ -3.5%, NVDA -4.2%) as risk appetite for AI-capex-heavy names wanes. In Singapore, the STI fell 1.4% with banks leading losses ahead of a heavy earnings week (UOB Nov 4, DBS Nov 5, OCBC Nov 6), and OCBC is under added pressure after its insurer subsidiary Great Eastern posted a 72% profit collapse.

picks.thesis: AWS delivered its fastest Q3 growth in nearly five years (+39% YoY revenue, +55% operating income), beating consensus, yet AMZN stock is down 15.4% over 3 months and trades 15% below its 52-week high. The disconnect between fundamental cloud acceleration and share price weakness looks like an overreaction to broader AI-capex jitters rather than Amazon-specific issues.
picks.news: AWS Q3 revenue $45.98B, up 39% YoY and above the $45.29B consensus, with operating income up 55% - fastest Q3 AWS growth in nearly five years (2026-10-29).
picks.risks: If AI capex concerns intensify further or AWS guidance for Q4 disappoints, the stock could continue to de-rate alongside the broader hyperscaler group; elevated rel_volume (2.75x) shows heavy selling pressure that could persist near-term.

picks.thesis: Keppel has the most bullish analyst skew on the watchlist (12 buy/2 hold/1 sell) with 26.5% implied upside to consensus target, after a 23.7% pullback from its 52-week high and a 9% 1-month decline. No negative company-specific catalyst in the news flow suggests this is sector/macro-driven weakness (STI consolidation) rather than a fundamental deterioration, setting up a mean-reversion opportunity.
picks.news: No fresh Keppel-specific news; broader STI consolidation below key support levels is the main macro backdrop dragging SGX names lower (2026-11-02).
picks.risks: Prolonged STI weakness or a broader risk-off mood tied to AI capex concerns could keep Keppel depressed regardless of fundamentals; thin news means the thesis rests mainly on analyst targets and technical oversold conditions.

picks.thesis: Google Cloud revenue surged 103% YoY to $30.7B, the strongest growth among the three major hyperscalers, yet GOOGL has been hit hardest of the group, down 17.3% in a month and 30.5% from its 52-week high. A recent analyst downgrade (Citizens) adds to near-term caution, but the scale of the cloud beat versus the scale of the selloff looks overdone for a company with 53 buy ratings and 45% implied upside to consensus target.
picks.news: Google Cloud revenue +103% YoY to $30.7B in Q3 2026 (2026-10-28); Citizens downgraded from Market Outperform to Market Perform on 2026-10-29, after which the stock moved -13.9%.
picks.risks: Continued AI capex scrutiny across the sector, or a disappointing guide on advertising/search amid AI disruption fears, could extend the downtrend; the recent downgrade signals some analysts see further risk.

picks.thesis: S&P Global just cut Meta's outlook to negative specifically over capex uncertainty ($135-145B annual spend) and free-cash-flow risk, a direct credit-market signal of rising financial risk. The stock is already down 15.3% in a month and 20.9% from its 52-week high, and today's broad AI-capex-driven selloff (QQQ -3.5%) hit Meta on the same day as the downgrade, reinforcing that sentiment is turning against aggressive AI spenders without AWS/Azure-style monetization visibility.
picks.news: S&P Global revised Meta's outlook from stable to negative on 2026-11-02, citing capex plans of $135-145B annually and FCF uncertainty.
picks.risks: If Meta's upcoming results show strong ad revenue growth or any sign of AI monetization (e.g., via Llama/enterprise tools) that offsets capex concerns, sentiment could reverse quickly; Meta still carries 55 buy ratings and 37.9% implied upside per consensus targets.

picks.thesis: NVDA fell 4.2% today alone and is down 11.4% over the past month, now trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a 14.5% drawdown from its 52-week high. As the poster child of AI capex, Nvidia is most exposed to any further wobble in hyperscaler spending sentiment, and its high beta (1.62) and elevated volatility (37.3%) mean it tends to amplify broader AI-capex-driven risk-off moves like today's.
picks.news: Broad AI-capex concern (Meta S&P downgrade 2026-11-02) coincided with a sharp NVDA drop and QQQ -3.5% today; no NVDA-specific negative news but it is the most capex-sensitive name on the watchlist.
picks.risks: Consensus target implies 60.7% upside and the stock has an overwhelmingly bullish analyst base (59 buy/2 hold/1 sell); any reassurance from hyperscalers on continued AI infrastructure spend (e.g., in upcoming earnings) could spark a sharp reversal higher.

picks.thesis: OCBC fell 3.3% today and is down 10.5% over the past month after its insurance subsidiary Great Eastern reported a 72% YoY profit collapse, raising concerns about OCBC's own Q3 results due November 6. With the stock already 12.2% below its 52-week high and trading below its 50-day MA, the insurance-arm weakness combined with broader STI consolidation creates near-term downside risk into the earnings date.
picks.news: Great Eastern (OCBC's insurance subsidiary) reported Q3 profit down 72% YoY to S$102.9M, pressuring OCBC shares ahead of its Nov 6 earnings (2026-11-02).
picks.risks: OCBC's banking core (ex-insurance) could still post resilient net interest income and loan growth, and with 8 buy ratings and 10.4% implied upside, a reassuring earnings print on Nov 6 could trigger a relief rally.
